items.name: Autovacuum and its settings
items.explanation: Autovacuum is a background process that vacuums tables for you. A few settings decide how many workers run, how often it wakes and how much it pauses to spare the server, so a busy database can set it to fall behind.

assumedBy.quote: Additionally, we had been running with far too much delay in vacuuming which meant lower load on the system, but more idle time in maintenance.

items.name: Postgres single-user mode
items.explanation: A Postgres server can be started with --single, which runs one session straight on the data directory with no other clients. It is the way to run VACUUM on a database that refuses normal connections.

assumedBy.quote: One piece of general advice is to stop the database and restart in single-user mode, thus running vacuum in a more isolated and safe environment.
When Postgres shuts down to protect against wraparound, it needs to be put into standalone mode and cleaned using the VACUUM command.

items.name: TRUNCATE versus DELETE
items.explanation: TRUNCATE empties a table without scanning its rows and gives the disk space back at once, where DELETE leaves dead rows for a later VACUUM. That is why it can finish quickly on a huge table.

assumedBy.quote: With our best estimations, we made the call to truncate the table.
After verifying that this would free the associated XIDs, we decided to truncate the tables.
